description: Customer-facing after-service care guidance for common TorqueMech repairs. This data is intentionally separate from UI and invoice templates.

engine_oil_and_filter_replacement.what_to_expect: The engine should sound and feel normal after service; a brief residual oil smell can occur if old oil was cleaned from nearby surfaces.
first_24_48_hours: Listen and feel for any new noises, vibration, warning lights, leaks, or odors.
Recheck the vehicle only when it is parked safely and components are cool where applicable.
Contact the shop promptly if the repair area shows active leakage or the vehicle feels unsafe.
normal_conditions: Slightly different feel after new parts or fresh fluid can be normal.
Minor residual odor can occur if old fluid or cleaner was present on exterior surfaces.
Electronic monitors, idle strategy, or shift adaptation may take normal driving time to settle on some vehicles.
warning_signs: the original symptom returns or worsens
unusual noise, smell, smoke, or vibration
customer_recommendations: Avoid severe operation immediately after service when practical, especially with brakes, tires, driveline, or fluid repairs.
Do not ignore warning lights, fluid loss, overheating, brake-pedal changes, fuel odor, or smoke.
Use the vehicle manufacturer maintenance schedule and the shop invoice notes for any vehicle-specific follow-up.
recheck_guidance: A short follow-up inspection is appropriate if a leak, noise, odor, vibration, warning light, or drivability concern appears.
Fluid-level rechecks should be performed with the correct temperature and procedure when the system requires it.
For raised-vehicle work, wheel fastener torque and undercarriage safety should be verified using proper equipment.
maintenance_guidance: Record the mileage and date of service.
Follow the next service interval based on manufacturer guidance, fluid condition, driving conditions, and inspection findings.
Plan related inspections before replacing additional parts unless test results support the added repair.
